whichever panel is currently focused (the first one when none is).

A workspace-wide concept rather than a per-panel one, like `watchlists` and `scripting`: one
assistant, pointed at whichever chart is in front. Forwarded verbatim to that panel's own
`CandlestickChart.ai` — see that prop for what it accepts, and for why an `apiKey` in a
browser is a decision to take deliberately.

brokers.name: brokers
brokers.description:
The brokers this workspace can trade through. Passing a non-empty list is what puts the plug
button on the right-hand rail — one button for the whole workspace, since a connection is to
an account and not to a panel.

**This library ships none.** Each entry is a `BrokerAdapter` the host implements: it declares
what its form asks for and carries every call that leaves the browser. See that interface for
why a front-end library must not be the thing holding credentials or signing orders.
`SAMPLE_BROKERS` in the test data is four fakes that answer from a file, for trying the flow
out.

brokerPnlToday.name: brokerPnlToday
brokerPnlToday.description:
The account's realised change today, from the host — what the daily-loss ceiling is checked
against. This library never sees a fill, so it cannot compute one, and a limit measured
against a number it invented would be worse than no limit. Absent, that ceiling never
triggers and the panel says so.

scripting.name: scripting
scripting.description:
Shows the rail's own "</>" button and shares *one* script list (and one editor) across every
panel — unlike every other `CandlestickChartProps` scripting prop, which stays per-panel for
a standalone chart, a workspace script explicitly targets one chosen panel (see
`ScriptDef.targetPanelIndex`'s own doc) rather than living inside any one panel's own state.
Default false.

SeasonalityView.description:
Presentational half of the seasonality feature — `computeSeasonality` (see
`internal/seasonality.ts`) does the actual aggregation, kept entirely independent of this
component (and of React) so it can be tested, reused, or extended on its own. The header holds
the back button, title, and the view-mode dropdown (Années indépendantes/Année en cours, the
latter also the default — see `SeasonalityViewMode`); granularity and the years filter live in
their own
left-docked icon rail instead — same `TOOLS_RAIL_WIDTH`/visual convention as
`CandlestickChart`'s own drawing-tools rail — each opening its own popover (`DropdownPanel` for
years, since a multi-select with its own bulk actions needs more than the plain option list a
`Select` gives). The chart body itself renders through
`LineAreaChart` rather than a bespoke chart of its own — a seasonal path is just one more line
series once it's been computed, no reason to re-implement axes/zoom/hover for it — told to
match the main chart's own right-side price-axis convention (`yAxisOrientation="right"`,
`margin` reserving the same rail width on its own left edge) and to drop its own border
(`embedded`) since it's nested inside CandlestickChart's own bordered root.

symbol.name: symbol
symbol.description:
Shown in the header, next to "— Saisonnalité" — same convention as the main chart's own
symbol label.

onBack.name: onBack
onBack.description: Returns to the regular (non-seasonality) chart body.

mobile.name: mobile
mobile.description:
Narrow/phone layout (see CandlestickChart's own `isNarrowLayout`). Only affects the price
axis' own width, which drops to the same PRICE_AXIS_WIDTH_MOBILE gutter the candle chart uses
there — so switching between the two views doesn't move the scale sideways under the reader.
Default false.

showHeader.name: showHeader
showHeader.description:
Same gate CandlestickChart's own header uses (`showHeader`) — without it there'd be no way
back out of seasonality mode, so this only ever hides the header in the same edge case the
main chart's own header would already be hidden in. Default true.

height.name: height
height.description: Fixed height in px for the chart area. Fills 100% of the container's width regardless.

thresholds.name: thresholds
thresholds.description: Color bands drawn as the track, e.g. [{upTo:33,color:'var(--lq-color-down)'}, {upTo:66,color:'var(--lq-color-warning)'}, {upTo:100,color:'var(--lq-color-up)'}].

showBandLabels.name: showBandLabels
showBandLabels.description:
Draws each threshold's own `label` (see GaugeThreshold — declared for exactly this, unused
until now) just outside the arc, at that band's own angular midpoint — e.g. "Vente forte" /
"Vente" / "Neutre" / "Achat" / "Achat fort" around a 5-band analyst-rating gauge. A band with
no `label` simply gets no text. Ignored without `thresholds` (there's no band to label a
midpoint of). Default false. Reserves extra room around the arc itself (see LABEL_MARGIN/
LABEL_TOP_MARGIN below) so the outermost labels don't clip the SVG's own edge — the arc stays
exactly `size` wide either way, only the surrounding canvas grows.

DonutChart.description: Allocation / breakdown donut, e.g. portfolio composition by asset class.

centerValue.name: centerValue
centerValue.description:
Overrides the center's own default (non-hovered) value/caption — e.g. a distinct-category
count ("5" over "Types de symboles") instead of the sum of every slice's own value / "Total".
Hovering a slice still shows that slice's own value/label as usual either way.

legendPosition.name: legendPosition
legendPosition.description: Where the legend renders relative to the plot itself. Default "bottom".

shape.name: shape
shape.description:
"circle" (default): the usual round donut. "square": each slice's own outer edge follows a
square frame instead of a circular arc (see `squareSlicePath`'s own doc) — same overall
footprint either way (the square's own corners reach exactly as far as the circle's edge
would have), just a different silhouette. The inner (hole) boundary stays circular in both.

WorldExposureMap.description:
Interactive world choropleth — each of the eight regions shaded by its own share of `data`
(see `matchContinent`), darker for a bigger share. Hover (mouse) or press-and-hold/tap (touch,
same unified Pointer Events every other chart in this library already uses for its own
hover — see DonutChart) shows that continent's own value in a floating tooltip.

data.name: data
data.description:
Arbitrary region labels, e.g. straight from the same `countBy(rows, r => r.region)` helper
a caller's own donut chart already uses — this component owns turning a label like "US" or
"Europe" into a continent (see `matchContinent`'s own doc), not the caller. A label that
doesn't resolve to any of the eight regions (e.g. "Global", or "Autre") contributes to the
small "Non localisable" note instead of coloring anything, rather than being silently
dropped.

MatrixChart.description:
A matrix of scored cells — a correlation grid being the case it was built for, though nothing
here assumes correlation beyond the default `[-1, 1]` domain.

Colour carries two separate facts and keeps them separate: the hue is the sign, the opacity is
the magnitude. A cell at +1 is the positive colour at full strength, a cell at 0 is transparent,
a cell at -1 is the negative colour at full strength. That is what makes the grid readable
without a legend: the eye reads "how much" from how loud a cell is and "which way" from which
colour it is, instead of having to place a shade along a continuous two-hue ramp.

Clicking a cell opens its detail underneath rather than in a tooltip. What a cell means usually
takes several lines, and a tooltip that has to be kept hovered is the wrong container for
anything somebody wants to sit and read.

domain.name: domain
domain.description:
The values mapped to a full negative and a full positive tint. Default `[-1, 1]`, which is
what a correlation runs between.

colorMode.name: colorMode
colorMode.description:
`"auto"` ramps the two colours below by opacity (see this component's own doc); `"manual"`
uses each cell's own `color` and leaves the ramp entirely to the caller.

showValues.name: showValues
showValues.description: Prints the value inside each cell.

zoomable.name: zoomable
zoomable.description:
Wheel to zoom, drag to pan, double-click to reset. Off leaves the matrix fixed — the right
choice when it already fits, since a grid that moves under an accidental scroll is worse
than one that cannot move at all.

type.name: func
type.raw: ((cell: MatrixCell, row: MatrixAxisEntry, column: MatrixAxisEntry) => ReactNode) | undefined

Heatmap.description:
Squarified-treemap "stock heatmap": stocks grouped by sector, each tile sized by one metric
(`value`) and colored by another (`colorValue`) — the classic pairing being market cap for
size, % change for color, though nothing here assumes that specifically. Click a group's own
header to drill into just it (filling the whole plot, with a breadcrumb back to "Tout"); click
a tile to report it via `onTileClick` instead — a tile has no children to drill into, so that
gesture reports outward (compose, don't configure: what "clicking a stock" should actually do,
loading it into a chart or anything else, is entirely up to the caller) rather than doing
anything to this component's own view state. Built on `useD3Zoom`, the same internal hook
every other zoomable chart in this library already shares — wheel-to-zoom already zooms
toward the cursor by construction (d3-zoom's own default behavior), nothing extra needed here
for that.

colorDomain.name: colorDomain
colorDomain.description:
[min, max] `colorValue` mapped to the fullest down/up color — anything past either end
clamps to it rather than extrapolating further. Default [-3, 3] (percent-change scale).

onTileClick.name: onTileClick
onTileClick.description: Fires when a *tile* (never a group — see this component's own doc for why) is clicked.

AlertsPanel.description:
Read-only(-ish) list of every alert set on the chart's own drawings/indicators — meant for
`ChartWorkspace`'s own "Alertes" side-panel tab (`alerts` prop), showing the same caller-owned
list `CandlestickChart` itself was handed (see its own `alerts` prop doc). Deleting is
self-contained (no modal needed); *editing* an alert stays scoped to the drawing/indicator's
own toolbar it was created from (see `AlertListModal`) — this panel is purely for visibility
across the whole chart, not a second place to edit from.

Sparkline.description: Minimal, axis-free trend line — for table cells, KPI cards, watchlists.

area.name: area
area.description: Fills the area under the line.

colorByTrend.name: colorByTrend
colorByTrend.description: Colors the line using the up/down theme tokens based on the first/last value delta.

DeltaChart.description:
Waterfall / bridge chart: shows how a sequence of signed additions and subtractions build up to
one or more totals — e.g. capital structure (market cap + debt + minority interest − cash = enterprise value).
Built on the same index-scale zoom/pan/axis-rescale primitives as `CandlestickChart`.

showConnectors.name: showConnectors
showConnectors.description: Dashed bridging lines between consecutive bars. Default true.

showValueAxis.name: showValueAxis
showValueAxis.description:
Shows the value axis (labels and axis line). `false` keeps only the grid (hover tooltip still gives each
amount). Default true.

hideYAxisLine.name: hideYAxisLine
hideYAxisLine.description:
Hides the vertical (Y) axis *line* while keeping its value labels and grid; the X axis line then runs on to
the SVG's own left edge (under the labels), as on a borderless card. Default false.

showYAxisLine.name: showYAxisLine
showYAxisLine.description:
Shows the vertical (Y) axis *line*. `false` hides only that line — values and grid stay, the X axis line is left
as is (see `extendXAxisLine` to run it on). Default true.

extendXAxisLine.name: extendXAxisLine
extendXAxisLine.description:
Runs the X axis line on past the Y axis, under its value labels, to the SVG's own left edge — with or without the
Y axis line. Default false.

zoomable.name: zoomable
zoomable.description:
Pan/zoom the categorical axis — same drag/wheel/axis-rescale conventions as
`CandlestickChart` and `LineAreaChart`, useful once there are many steps. Default true.

fullscreenToggle.name: fullscreenToggle
fullscreenToggle.description: Shows a fullscreen toggle button in the toolbar. Default true.

embedded.name: embedded
embedded.description:
Drops the chart's own outer border, for a chart that sits inside a container already
drawing one (a card, a panel, a dashboard cell). Same flag and same effect as
`LineAreaChart.embedded`. Default false.

ChartTooltip.description:
Floating box positioned in pixel-space over a chart's plot area (absolute, parent must be
`position: relative`).

Its placement is computed here rather than left to a CSS margin, because it has to know two
things CSS cannot tell it: how big the box came out, and how big the plot is. The rule it
replaces was "flip to the left past 65% of the width", which never measured either — so a box
wider than the space its own flip left it ran straight off the left edge and took its text with
it. Measured on a 300px gallery tile: 96px of a 160px box outside the plot. The vertical axis is
clamped the same way and for the same reason.

`useLayoutEffect`, so the correction lands before the browser paints and the box never appears
in the wrong place first.

align.name: align
align.description:
Which side of `x` the box prefers. It is a preference, not a position: a box that would leave
the plot is pulled back inside whichever side it was asked for. Default "right".

ChartAxis.description:
Thin React wrapper around d3-axis: d3 owns the tick DOM inside a single
`<g>`, React owns everything else. This is the one place components in
this file "hand off" to imperative D3, which is the idiomatic way to mix
the two without them fighting over the same nodes.

tickValues.name: tickValues
tickValues.description:
Explicit tick positions, e.g. one per visible bar on an index-based categorical axis.
Overrides the automatic `ticks` count when provided.

domainExtent.name: domainExtent
domainExtent.description:
Overrides where the domain *line* itself starts and ends, in the axis group's own local
coordinates (the same space as `scale.range()`, which is what it defaults to). For an axis
whose scale is deliberately ranged to less than the box it belongs to — a docked column's own
price axis reserves room at the top of its range so plotted values clear the pane header, see
`usePaneStackScales`'s own `headerReserve` — this keeps the drawn line spanning the full box
while ticks and data still land on the (shorter) scale.

gridLength.name: gridLength
gridLength.description: Length of grid lines (usually the plot's bounded width/height). Required when `grid` is true.

className.name: className
className.description: Extra class on the axis group (e.g. `lq-chart__axis--hidden`: grid lines only, no labels or axis line).

SankeyChart.description:
Sankey diagram — where a quantity comes from and where it ends up, drawn as ribbons whose
thickness is the quantity itself.

Three things make it worth interacting with rather than just looking at:

- **the wheel adds detail, not just size.** Labels appear as their node becomes tall enough on
  screen to carry one, and each label grows from a name, to a name and a figure, to a name, a
  figure and its share of what feeds it. Zoomed out you read the shape; zoomed in you read the
  numbers. Text is drawn outside the zoom transform, so it stays at its own size throughout —
  magnified type would give more pixels and no more information.
- **clicking a node flies to its branch.** Everything downstream of it is framed, everything
  off that path is dimmed, and the trail of clicks is kept in the toolbar so you can walk back
  out. A budget's leaves are unreadably thin at full extent; this is how you get to them.
- **hovering says what a ribbon is worth**, including its share of the node it leaves, which is
  the question a Sankey is usually being asked.

The layout is this library's own (`internal/sankeyLayout.ts`) rather than `d3-sankey` — see that
file for why.

nodeWidth.name: nodeWidth
nodeWidth.description: Width of a node's bar in px. Default 12.

nodePadding.name: nodePadding
nodePadding.description:
Vertical gap between two nodes of the same column, in px. Default 14 — a ceiling, not a
promise: a column of twenty leaves would spend the whole chart on gaps, so the layout narrows
it as far as it needs to keep half the height for the flows themselves.

align.name: align
align.description:
`"justify"` (default) lines every terminal node up on the right-hand edge — what a budget
diagram wants. `"left"` leaves each node in the column its longest incoming path gives it.

zoomable.name: zoomable
zoomable.description: Wheel to zoom, drag to pan, click a node to fly to its branch. Default true.

scaleExtent.name: scaleExtent
scaleExtent.description:
[min, max] zoom factor. Default [1, 14] — the upper end is what makes the deepest, thinnest
ribbons of a real budget separable.

fullscreenToggle.name: fullscreenToggle
fullscreenToggle.description: Shows a fullscreen toggle in the toolbar. Default true.

embedded.name: embedded
embedded.description:
Drops the chart's own outer border, for a chart already inside something that draws one.
Same flag and effect as `LineAreaChart.embedded`. Default false.

onNodeClick.name: onNodeClick
onNodeClick.description: Fires in addition to — not instead of — the built-in zoom-to-branch.

InteractiveGlobe.description:
A rotating, zoomable 3D globe that draws points, great-circle flows and animated particles on
the GPU.

The component knows nothing about what the data *means*: it takes points with coordinates and
arcs between them, and hands back ids when the user interacts. Everything domain-shaped — what a
node is, what a flow represents, what should happen on click — stays in the consuming product.
That boundary is what lets the same renderer drive an economic-dependency map, a logistics
dashboard and a network-latency view without forking.

Rendering is WebGL and lives entirely outside React: the component mounts two canvases and an
engine, then pushes prop changes into it. React re-renders here cost one diff of an empty div —
they never touch the frame loop.

nodes.name: nodes
nodes.description: Points on the sphere. Also the lookup table flows use when they name endpoints by id.

flows.name: flows
flows.description: Great-circle arcs between nodes or raw coordinates, optionally carrying particles.

markers.name: markers
markers.description: Secondary points drawn above the flows (cities, events, infrastructure…).

autoRotate.name: autoRotate
autoRotate.description: Spins the globe until the user touches it, then resumes a couple of seconds later.

autoRotateSpeed.name: autoRotateSpeed
autoRotateSpeed.description: Degrees of longitude per second. Default 4.

animateFlows.name: animateFlows
animateFlows.description: Set false to keep the arcs but stop every particle. Default true.

quality.name: quality
quality.description: Rendering budget — dot density and whether particles run at all. Default "high".

maxAnimatedFlows.name: maxAnimatedFlows
maxAnimatedFlows.description: Hard cap on how many flows may carry particles at once. Default 90.

particleScale.name: particleScale
particleScale.description: Multiplies the diameter of the particles travelling along each flow. Default 1.

countryHover.name: countryHover
countryHover.description:
Outlines the country under the pointer, and reports it through `onCountryHover`. Default true.

Turning it off skips loading the country outlines entirely, which is worth doing for a globe
whose subject is not geography — a satellite track, say, where a highlighted Chad is noise.

labelMode.name: labelMode
labelMode.description: "auto" thins labels to fit the zoom tier; "all" draws every one. Default "auto".

theme.name: theme
theme.description: Colors. Every entry accepts any CSS color and defaults to a `--lq-*` token.

initialView.name: initialView
initialView.description: Camera position on first mount. Changing it afterwards does nothing — use the ref.

selectedNodeId.name: selectedNodeId
selectedNodeId.description: Drawn with a ring, and used to dim everything it does not touch.

highlightedFlowIds.name: highlightedFlowIds
highlightedFlowIds.description: Flows lifted out of the dimming, e.g. the steps of a scenario being played back.

interactive.name: interactive
interactive.description: Set false for a decorative globe: no drag, no zoom, no hit-testing. Default true.

onCountryHover.name: onCountryHover

type.name: func
type.raw: ((country: GlobeCountryRef | null, x: number, y: number) => void) | undefined

onCountryHover.description: Fires when the pointer crosses into another country, or out to open water (`null`).

onCountryClick.name: onCountryClick

type.name: func
type.raw: ((country: GlobeCountryRef, x: number, y: number) => void) | undefined

onCountryClick.description:
Fires when a click lands on a landmass that is not already a node or a flow.

`country.nodeIds` names the nodes standing inside it, so a consumer can map the click onto its
own entities without keeping a country-code table of its own. Takes precedence over
`onBackgroundClick`, which now means "clicked the ocean".

onBackgroundClick.name: onBackgroundClick
onBackgroundClick.description: Fired for a click that hit neither a node nor a flow — the usual "clear selection" hook.

onViewChange.name: onViewChange
onViewChange.description: Throttled: only fires past half a degree of rotation or a 1% zoom change.

overlay.name: overlay
overlay.description:
Absolutely-positioned content above the canvases (HUD, legend, tooltip). Not hit-testable
unless a child opts back in with `pointer-events: auto`.

fallback.name: fallback
fallback.description: Shown instead of the globe when the browser has no WebGL.

ariaLabel.name: ariaLabel
ariaLabel.description: Accessible name for the canvas region.

width.name: width
width.description:
Size in CSS pixels. Omit either one and the map measures its own container for that dimension
and fills it, re-measuring as the container changes.

Filling needs the parent to have a size of its own: a `height: 100%` inside a box that is only
as tall as its contents resolves to nothing, and the map would draw at zero height. Give the
container a height — a viewport unit, a grid row, a flex child with `min-height: 0` — or pass
`height` outright.

center.name: center
center.description: Starting centre. The map owns its camera afterwards — see the note on `center`.

tileUrl.name: tileUrl
tileUrl.description:
Tile template with `{z}`, `{x}`, `{y}`, and optionally `{s}` for a subdomain.

Read once per render rather than memoised: changing it swaps the basemap, which is exactly the
case a consumer switching between a light and a dark style needs to work.

attribution.name: attribution
attribution.description: Shown bottom-right. Required by the ODbL for OpenStreetMap data — see the component's doc.

tileFilter.name: tileFilter
tileFilter.description:
CSS filter applied to the tiles, overriding the one the palette would choose.

The annotations are drawn after it and are never filtered: a marker whose colour a consumer
chose must arrive on screen as that colour, whatever is being done to the basemap underneath.

routes.name: routes
routes.description:
Lines drawn over the basemap: an itinerary and the alternatives offered alongside it.

Every route is drawn with a casing in the surface colour underneath its own stroke. That is
not decoration — a coloured line laid straight onto a basemap disappears wherever it crosses
something of a similar tone, and a road map is nothing but similar tones. The casing is what
makes one line readable over motorway, water and city alike.

selectedRouteId.name: selectedRouteId
selectedRouteId.description:
The chosen route. Everything else in `routes` is drawn as an alternative — thinner, muted,
and underneath, so the choice is legible at a glance rather than by reading the legend.

onRouteSelect.name: onRouteSelect
onRouteSelect.description:
Fires on a click on a route's line or on its badge. Pair it with `selectedRouteId` to let
someone switch itinerary on the map itself, the way the badges invite.

onViewChange.name: onViewChange

type.name: func
type.raw: ((view: { lon: number; lat: number; zoom: number; }) => void) | undefined

onViewChange.description: Fires after every pan and zoom, coarsely — not on every animation frame.

DotMap.description:
Carte du monde en pointillés : la terre dessinée par une grille régulière de points, des repères
dessus, et une infobulle au clic sur un repère — le bloc « géolocalisation » d'un tableau de bord.

Les terres viennent du même `world-atlas` que `WorldExposureMap`. Projection, cadrage (`bounds`,
ou `center` et `zoom`), pas et taille des points se règlent ; les couleurs suivent le thème, ou le
`tone` qui remplit la carte. Les points sont un seul tracé SVG — des segments de longueur nulle à
bouts ronds ou carrés —, si bien que leur couleur reste une variable CSS et que des milliers de
points ne pèsent qu'un élément.

Les repères sont des boutons : ils se prennent au clavier, Entrée ouvre l'infobulle, Échap la
ferme. L'infobulle est hors de la surface colorée, pour garder les couleurs ordinaires du panneau.

width.name: width
width.description: Largeur en px. Par défaut, toute la largeur du conteneur, suivie quand il change de taille.

projection.name: projection
projection.description:
Projection : un nom, ou une fabrique de projection d3 (`() => d3.geoAlbers()`) — définie hors du
rendu, sans quoi la grille est recalculée à chaque rendu. Défaut : `"naturalEarth"`.

bounds.name: bounds
bounds.description:
Région à cadrer : `[[ouest, sud], [est, nord]]`, en degrés. Elle tient entière dans la carte, la
terre alentour remplit le reste. Par défaut, le monde entier.

center.name: center
center.description: Point placé au centre de la carte, après le cadrage.

zoom.name: zoom
zoom.description: Grossissement appliqué après le cadrage, autour de `center`. Défaut : 1.

dotSpacing.name: dotSpacing
dotSpacing.description: Pas de la grille de points, en px. Défaut : 6.

dotSize.name: dotSize
dotSize.description: Diamètre (ou côté) d'un point, en px. Défaut : 3.

background.name: background
background.description:
Couleur de fond (toute couleur CSS, `var(--lq-…)` compris). Par défaut, celle du panneau, ou le
remplissage du `tone`.

dotColor.name: dotColor
dotColor.description: Couleur des points. Par défaut, le texte à 30 % ; à 70 % sur un `tone`.

tone.name: tone
tone.description:
Remplit la carte d'une couleur du thème et passe les points en contraste — voir `SurfaceTone`.
Défaut : `"default"`.

antarctica.name: antarctica
antarctica.description: Garde l'Antarctique dans la grille. Défaut : false.

pulse.name: pulse
pulse.description: Halo animé autour des repères (coupé par `prefers-reduced-motion`). Défaut : true.

selectedId.name: selectedId
selectedId.description: Repère dont l'infobulle est ouverte (contrôlé) ; `null` pour aucun.

label.name: label
label.description: Nom de la carte pour les lecteurs d'écran. Défaut : « Carte ».

Popover.description:
Low-level anchored floating panel: portals to `document.body`, positions
itself with collision detection (see `usePopoverPosition`), and closes on
outside click / Escape. Powers `Select`, `DatePicker`, and any menu-style
dropdown built on top of this library.

placement.name: placement
placement.description: Preferred side; flips to the other side (and shifts horizontally) when there isn't room.

matchAnchorWidth.name: matchAnchorWidth
matchAnchorWidth.description: Match the panel's width to the anchor's width (typical for a Select).

trackKey.name: trackKey
trackKey.description:
Re-measure whenever this changes — for an anchor that moves without the page scrolling or
resizing, such as an element on a canvas being panned, zoomed or dragged. See
`usePopoverPosition`.

Select.description:
Adapted dropdown select: opens below the trigger by default, flips above
and shifts horizontally when the viewport doesn't have room (see `Popover`).

Input.description:
Base text input: label, leading/trailing icon slots, and an error state that
every other form control in this library (Select, MaskedInput, DatePicker) shares visually.

InputNumber.description:
Numeric input with optional +/- steppers and a prefix/suffix (currency, percent…). Every value
this can ever actually produce — typed, pasted, or via the steppers — is rounded to 4 decimal
places (see round4's own doc) before reaching `onChange`, so a caller never has to guard
against float noise on its own end.

A plain text input under the hood, not `type="number"`: a native number input's own displayed
text is locale-formatted by the browser itself — under French, typing "." is silently redrawn
as "," (confirmed bug report), and there is no way for this component to opt out of that from
the outside. Rendering as text and parsing by hand (see normalizeDecimal) sidesteps it
entirely — what's typed is what's shown, "." and "," both parse, and the displayed value is
never at the mercy of whatever locale the browser happens to be running under.

DatePicker.description:
Calendar popup date field, positioned via the same adaptive `Popover` engine as `Select`. Click the
"month year" header to drill up to a month grid, then a year grid — much faster than paging
month-by-month to change years.

DateRangePicker.description:
Same calendar popup as `DatePicker`, but for picking a start/end pair — like booking a
stay from date A to date B. First click sets the start; hovering afterwards previews the
span up to the cursor; second click sets the end (swapped automatically if it lands before
the start) and closes. Clicking again after a complete range starts a fresh selection.

DateTimePicker.description:
`DatePicker` plus a time-of-day panel next to the calendar — an opt-in separate component
so the plain date-only `DatePicker` stays untouched. Picking a day doesn't close the popover
(the time still needs setting); "Valider" commits the combined date+time and closes.

minuteStep.name: minuteStep
minuteStep.description:
Increment (minutes) between entries in the scrollable time list. Default 15. An exact
time off this grid can still be typed directly into the time input.

RangeSlider.description:
Dual-handle range picker — e.g. a price/date range filter. Drag either handle to resize
the range, or drag the filled segment between them to shift the whole range at once.

centerZero.name: centerZero
centerZero.description:
Marks 0 on the track and colors the fill negative/positive on either side of it —
for a "min/max is negative left, positive right" filter. Requires `min < 0 < max`.

Tag/chip input: type and press comma or Enter to add a tag, Backspace on an empty field to drop the last one, or

WysiwygEditor.description:
Rich-text editor: a toolbar over a contenteditable document, themed like every other field in
this kit.

It is built on `document.execCommand`, which is formally deprecated and which every browser
still implements — deliberately. The alternative is a document model of one's own (ProseMirror,
Slate, Lexical), which is a dependency several times the size of this entire library and a
second, parallel idea of what a document *is*. What this component is for — a note, a
description, a comment next to a chart — is served by the browser's own editing engine, and the
value it produces is plain HTML rather than a proprietary document tree.

The toolbar never takes focus (every control cancels its own mousedown, and the block dropdown,
which does focus, restores the saved range before acting), so the selection you are looking at
is always the one a command applies to.

value.name: value
value.description:
The document, as an HTML string. Controlled if given — but only *loosely*: the editor is a
contenteditable element, and writing its `innerHTML` back on every keystroke would destroy the
caret, so incoming values are only applied when they differ from what this editor last
emitted. Pass a value that came from `onChange` and nothing moves; pass a different one (a
loaded draft, a reset) and the document is replaced.

It is set as `innerHTML`: whatever you pass is rendered as markup. Sanitise anything that came
from somewhere other than this editor before handing it over — this component does not, and
cannot usefully guess what you consider safe.

defaultValue.name: defaultValue
defaultValue.description: Initial document for an uncontrolled editor. Ignored once `value` is given.

onChange.name: onChange
onChange.description: Fires on every edit with the document's HTML.

placeholder.name: placeholder
placeholder.description: Shown centred in the empty document.

toolbar.name: toolbar
toolbar.description:
Which controls the toolbar carries, grouped — see `WYSIWYG_DEFAULT_TOOLBAR`. An empty array
hides the toolbar entirely, which with `readOnly` turns this into a plain rich-text viewer.

minHeight.name: minHeight
minHeight.description: Minimum height of the writing area in px. Default 180.

maxHeight.name: maxHeight
maxHeight.description:
Height at which the writing area stops growing and starts scrolling. Unset by default — the
editor grows with its content.

pasteAsPlainText.name: pasteAsPlainText
pasteAsPlainText.description:
Paste drops every bit of incoming formatting and inserts plain text. On by default: pasting
from a web page otherwise drags in its fonts, colours and sizes, which is exactly what a kit
with a theme of its own does not want. Set false for a native rich paste.

readOnly.description: Renders the document without a toolbar and without letting anyone edit it.

InputDropdown.description:
A text input combined with a dropdown list (combobox): typing filters the options as you go,
arrow keys move through them, Enter picks, Escape closes and restores the current value. Built on
the same `Popover` and field styles as `Select`, so the two read as one family. For a server-side
search, pass `filter={false}`, run the query from `onInputChange` and feed the results back
through `options` (with `loading` while it runs).

type.name: other

How typed text filters the list. Default: case- and accent-insensitive match on the label,
description and value. Pass `false` when the caller filters the options itself (results of a
server search driven by `onInputChange`) — the list is then shown as given.

onInputChange.name: onInputChange
onInputChange.description: Fired on every keystroke with the typed text (e.g. to run a server search).

emptyMessage.description: Shown when nothing matches. Default "Aucun résultat".

onClear.name: onClear
onClear.description: Shows a clear button while a value is selected.

maxResults.name: maxResults
maxResults.description: Caps how many options are rendered after filtering (long lists stay fast). Default 200.

ProgressBar.description:
Linear progress indicator — determinate (`value` set) or indeterminate (`value` omitted, an
animated stripe). `label`/the optional numeric read-out (`showValue`) can each independently
land on any of the bar's four edges or overlay it directly (`labelPosition`/`valuePosition`) —
from a plain loading bar with a caption above it (the default, and this component's original
shape) to a compact metrics row (label left, value right) or a value centered inside a thicker
bar.

value.name: value
value.description: 0-100. Omit for an indeterminate bar. Ignored once `segments` is set.

segments.name: segments
segments.description:
Splits the bar into multiple proportional colored sections side by side instead of a single
fill — a sector-allocation/budget-breakdown bar rather than a plain progress meter. Takes
over from `value`/`showValue` entirely when set (there's no single "percent done" once the
bar represents several parts of a whole at once) — `label`/`labelPosition` still work
normally alongside it, for an overall caption.

labelPosition.name: labelPosition
labelPosition.description:
Where `label` renders relative to the bar — "inside" overlays it centered on the track, in a
color that stays readable over both the filled and unfilled portions (see
`.lq-progress-bar__inside`'s own doc for how). Default "top", the original (and only)
position this component had before `labelPosition`/`valuePosition` existed.

showValue.name: showValue
showValue.description:
Shows a numeric read-out of `value` alongside/on the bar — off by default (the original
behavior had no separate value read-out at all; a caller wanting the number had to fold it
into `label` itself). Meaningless while indeterminate (no percentage to show), and quietly
ignored then regardless of this flag.

valuePosition.name: valuePosition
valuePosition.description:
Same five positions as `labelPosition`, independent of it — the two can share a position
(rendered side by side there) or sit on opposite edges. Default "right".

thickness.name: thickness
thickness.description:
Track height in px. Default 6 (the original, only size this component ever had) — fill/
segments always stay `height: 100%` of the track, so they thicken along with it automatically.

bordered.name: bordered
bordered.description:
Whether the track shows a border — omit to keep the palette's own existing default (only
"eink" gets one automatically, every other palette relies on the fill/track color contrast
alone); set explicitly to force it on or off regardless of palette, including overriding
eink's own otherwise-automatic border.

Stepper.description:
A sequence of steps threaded on a line: small filled squares the line runs straight through,
each with its own text, horizontally or vertically.

Every part of it fades by position rather than by colour — the current step at full strength,
what is behind it dimmer, what is ahead dimmest — and the line is cut into one independent
segment per gap so it fades the same way, brightening up to the current square and staying pale
past it. The line starts at the very edges: a leading segment before the first square and a
trailing one after the last, so the track spans the full width (or height) rather than stopping
at the outer squares.

active.name: active
active.description:
Index of the step currently in progress. `steps.length` means every step is behind us —
nothing is active any more and the whole line, trailing tail included, reads as travelled.

orientation.name: orientation
orientation.description:
Default "horizontal". Vertical puts the label *beside* the square rather than under it: the
space under a square in a vertical stepper is where the line to the next step runs, and text
dropped there would sit on top of it.

markerSize.name: markerSize
markerSize.description:
Side of the squares, in px. Default 12. The line is centred on this, so changing it moves the
line with it.

activeOpacity.name: activeOpacity
activeOpacity.description: Opacity of the current step. Default 1 — everything else is measured down from it.

completedOpacity.name: completedOpacity
completedOpacity.description:
Opacity of the steps already passed, and of the line segments leading to the current one.
Default 0.55: dimmer than the active step (which is what "only the current one is at full
strength" asks for) but clearly above the steps still to come, so the eye can still read how
far along the sequence is — a single dim level for both sides would show progress on the
squares' colours and nowhere else.

upcomingOpacity.name: upcomingOpacity
upcomingOpacity.description: Opacity of the steps still ahead, and of the line segments leading to them. Default 0.22.

stepSize.name: stepSize
stepSize.description:
Minimum length of one step along the line, in px (a row's height when vertical, a column's
width when horizontal). Default 56 vertical / 0 horizontal — a horizontal stepper already
gets its width from its container and only needs a floor when its labels are very short.

onClose.name: onClose
onClose.description: Fermer la visite — par la croix, « Passer la visite », Échap, ou à la fin.

onFinish.name: onFinish
onFinish.description: La visite est allée jusqu'au bout (le bouton final). Appelé avant `onClose`.

initialIndex.name: initialIndex
initialIndex.description: L'étape par laquelle commencer, à l'ouverture.

sort.name: sort
sort.description: Trier par gravité, les critiques d'abord. Défaut : oui.

emptyText.name: emptyText
emptyText.description: Ce qu'on affiche quand il n'y a rien. Défaut : rien du tout.

BalanceControl.description:
Left/right balance — one handle on a track with a detent at dead centre, and a fill that runs
*from the middle out* rather than from the left edge, so the picture is "how far off centre",
which is the only thing a balance says.

Double-click (or Home) recentres.

leftLabel.name: leftLabel
leftLabel.description: What the two ends are called. Default "L" and "R".

formatValue.name: formatValue
formatValue.description:
Formats the read-out. The default says which side it is leaning to rather than printing a
signed number, because "−34" does not say "left" to anyone who has not read the prop doc.

detent.name: detent
detent.description:
How close to the centre the handle has to come before it snaps there, in units. Default 4.
A real balance pot has a detent at the middle and it is the only way to reliably find dead
centre by hand; without one, a dragged handle lands on −1 or +2 and stays there. Pass 0 for a
perfectly linear control.

LevelMeter.description:
Signal level meters — one bar per channel, with held peaks, a hot zone, a clip light and an
optional dB scale.

Deliberately a *display*: it takes the numbers it is given and draws them. Ballistics — how
fast the bar falls, how long a peak is held — belong to whatever is producing the signal, and
every audio host already has its own opinion about them; a meter that invented its own would
disagree with the thing it is metering.

orientation.name: orientation
orientation.description: Default "vertical", the shape a mixer strip has.

range.name: range
range.description:
[floor, ceiling] in dBFS. Default [-60, 0] — below −60 there is nothing anyone acts on, and
0 is full scale by definition. Pass [0, 100] for a percentage meter and set `unit` to "".

warnAt.name: warnAt
warnAt.description: Level from which the meter reads as hot. Default −6 dB.

clipAt.name: clipAt
clipAt.description: Level from which it reads as clipping, and at which the clip light comes on. Default −1 dB.

segments.name: segments
segments.description:
How many blocks the bar is cut into; 0 draws it continuous. Default 24.

Blocks rather than a smooth gradient by default, for two reasons that happen to agree: a
segmented meter is the one everybody has already learnt to read, and under the e-ink palette
— where the warn and clip colours collapse into the same ink as everything else — the block
count is the only thing left that says how loud it is.

showScale.name: showScale
showScale.description: Draws the dB scale alongside. Default false.

showValue.name: showValue
showValue.description: Draws each channel's current figure. Default false.

thickness.name: thickness
thickness.description: Bar thickness in px (width when vertical, height when horizontal). Default 10.

length.name: length
length.description: Bar length in px. Default 140 vertical / 100 % of the container horizontal.

Equalizer.description:
Graphic equaliser — one fader per frequency band, over a dB grid, with the resulting response
drawn through the handles.

Double-click a fader (or Home) flattens that band; the "Réinitialiser" affordance is left to
the caller, since "flat" is not always the preset someone wants to get back to.

onChange.name: onChange
onChange.description:
Receives the whole next array — same shape as `RangeSlider`'s own `onChange`, so wiring one
to `useState` is a single line. Omit for a read-only response display.

range.name: range
range.description: Gain range, ± this many dB. Default 12.

unit.name: unit
unit.description: Printed under the frequency labels once, not on every band. Default "Hz".

height.name: height
height.description: Height of the fader columns in px. Default 150.

showCurve.name: showCurve
showCurve.description:
Joins the handles with a smooth curve — the response the settings add up to, which is the
thing an equaliser is actually for and which a row of independent faders does not show.
Default true.

showScale.name: showScale
showScale.description: dB gridlines behind the faders. Default true.

showValues.name: showValues
showValues.description:
Each band's own figure above its fader. Default false — with eight bands it is a wall of
numbers, and the curve already says the shape.

Scheduler.description:
A resource timeline: one row per machine or person, time across, and the jobs booked on them as
blocks you can drag, drop onto another row, and pull by either end.

## Overlaps grow the row

Two jobs booked on one machine at the same time is exactly what somebody opens a planner to
find, so they are never drawn on top of one another: the row splits into lanes and the clash is
visible as two bars side by side, marked. Hiding one behind the other would make the board
quietest precisely where it should be loudest.

## The wheel zooms the time axis

As it does on every other canvas in this kit, anchored on the pointer so the moment under the
cursor stays under it. That is a trade and worth naming: a board is also a table, and a table's
wheel normally scrolls it — so scrolling the rows moves to `Maj` + wheel, the scrollbar, or a
drag. `wheelZoom={false}` swaps the two back for a board long enough that reading down it
matters more than zooming across it.

## Clicking a task opens it

The block carries a name and, if there is room, a duration; everything else — description,
exact times, pattern, the steps it breaks into — lives in its dialog. A bar an inch tall has
room for a name, and a board that tried to show more on it would be legible only on its two
longest tasks.

onTasksChange.name: onTasksChange
onTasksChange.description:
Receives the whole next list, like every other controlled component here. Omit it for a
read-only board — nothing becomes draggable and no resize handles appear.

from.name: from
from.description: The window shown, as epoch ms or `Date`.

now.name: now
now.description: Drawn as a vertical marker. Omit for a plan with no "today" — a template, a scenario.

snapMinutes.name: snapMinutes
snapMinutes.description:
Everything a drag produces is rounded to this. Default 15 minutes. A schedule snapped to the
minute is a schedule nobody can line two tasks up in.

pxPerHour.name: pxPerHour
pxPerHour.description: Starting zoom. Default 60 px for an hour.

laneHeight.name: laneHeight
laneHeight.description: Row height per lane, in px. Default 34. A row with two overlapping tasks is two lanes tall.

resourceWidth.name: resourceWidth
resourceWidth.description: Width of the resource column. Default 168.

wheelZoom.name: wheelZoom
wheelZoom.description:
A plain wheel zooms the time axis; `Maj` + wheel scrolls the rows. Default true.

It is worth knowing what this trades: a board is a table, and a table's wheel normally scrolls
it. With this on, a list of forty machines is scrolled with `Maj`, the scrollbar, or a drag.
Set it false to get the table behaviour back — plain wheel scrolls, `Ctrl` zooms.

taskDialog.name: taskDialog
taskDialog.description: Opens the task's own dialog on click. Needs `onTasksChange` to be of any use. Default true.

SchedulerTaskModal.description:
A task's own dialog: what it is, when it runs, how it is drawn, and the steps it breaks into.

Everything commits as it is typed. There is no Save, for the same reason the warehouse's
inspector has none — the board is behind the dialog and moves with the edit, so a change you
cannot see until you confirm it is a change you have to guess at. `Escape` closes; nothing is
pending when it does.

The one thing this dialog will not let you express is a task whose parts do not add up to the
task. Segment lengths are the authority once a task has segments (see `SchedulerTask.subtasks`),
so editing one moves the task's end rather than leaving a discrepancy to be noticed later.

Badge.description: Small status pill — order/position state, KYC status, alert severity…

PriceChangeTag.description: Signed delta with an up/down arrow — price change, P&L, allocation drift.

StatCard.description: KPI tile: label, big value, optional caption, delta and trend sparkline.

delta.name: delta
delta.description: Signed delta rendered as a `PriceChangeTag` under the value.

caption.name: caption
caption.description: A muted line under the value — what the figure is made of, e.g. "fond 60 · machines 35 · froid 17".

HighlightStatCard.description:
Quiet KPI tile — thick top rule, muted label, big value, short subtext, trailing sparkline —
for a single standout stat (52-week high/low, all-time high…) rather than a boxed card.
Built on the `Highlight` primitive; unlike `StatCard` (delta tag + icon in a bordered `Panel`),
this has no box or delta pill, just the rule and the numbers themselves.

label.name: label
label.description:
Small muted uppercase label, e.g. "52-week high" (`Highlight` uppercases it via CSS — pass
normal case).

subtext.name: subtext
subtext.description: Short line under the value, e.g. "3,6 % en dessous".

HoldingCard.description: Compact row card for a single position — watchlists, holdings lists.

ComparisonCard.description: Two figures side by side with a divider — a portfolio vs. its benchmark, this period vs. last.

GaugeCard.description: A `GaugeChart` inside a titled card — risk score, goal progress, allocation drift.

Avatar.description: Circular avatar: image if `src` is given, otherwise initials from `name`.

Breadcrumbs.description: Path trail; the last item renders as the current, non-interactive page.

DataTable.description: Sortable, responsive (horizontally scrollable) data table — holdings, orders, transactions.

Notification.description:
Self-contained, fully controlled notification: pass `open`/`onClose` directly, no provider needed.
Great for a single persistent banner or one-off alert. For a queue of transient messages, use
`NotificationProvider` + `useNotification()` instead — it stacks multiple corner/bar notifications correctly.

variant.name: variant
variant.description: "corner" (default) — a popin anchored to one of the 4 corners. "bar" — a full-width sticky bar. "modal" — a centered dialog with an overlay.

actions.name: actions
actions.description:
Buttons row, e.g. "Annuler" / "Voir" — a plain link (e.g. "Lire la suite" on a news card,
see `NotificationSource`) works here too, not just `<button>`s.

meta.name: meta
meta.description:
Small text rendered opposite `actions` on the same row, e.g. a timestamp ("22:03") — omit
for no footer row at all when `actions` is also unset.

dismissible.name: dismissible
dismissible.description: Shows a close (×) button. Default true.

autoDismissMs.name: autoDismissMs
autoDismissMs.description: Auto-close after this many ms. Omit or pass 0 to require manual dismissal.

showProgress.name: showProgress
showProgress.description: Countdown progress bar while auto-dismissing. Default true whenever `autoDismissMs` is set.

onClick.name: onClick
onClick.description:
Makes the whole card clickable (e.g. "take me to the alert/article this is about"): called on a
click or Enter/Space anywhere on the card except its close button and `actions`, then the card
closes.

NotificationProvider.description:
Wrap your app (or a layout) once; call `useNotification().notify(...)` anywhere below it. Stacks
multiple corner/bar notifications correctly (unlike rendering several standalone `<Notification>`s).

NotificationSource.description:
A small "badges + source name" row — for a news-style notification's own byline, placed as (part of) `description` above the headline itself. Doesn't render a card of its own; it's meant to be composed into a regular `notify({ title, description: <>... })` call, e.g.: `description: <>

{headline}

`.

badges.name: badges
badges.description:
Small badges shown before the source name — logos, verification marks, ratings; their
content and meaning are entirely up to the caller, this just lays them out in a row.

UserMenu.description: Avatar + name trigger opening an adaptive dropdown menu — the usual header/sidebar account switcher.

NotificationMenu.description:
La cloche d'une barre d'application et sa liste déroulante : un bouton-icône avec une pastille de
non-lus, qui ouvre sous lui un panneau de notifications — icône ou avatar, titre, texte,
horodatage et point non-lu par ligne, avec en-tête, pied (« Tout marquer comme lu ») et état vide.

Le panneau est un `Popover` : il passe par un portail, se replace pour rester dans la fenêtre et se
ferme au clic extérieur ou sur Échap. À l'ouverture il prend le focus, pour qu'on y entre au
clavier sans traverser toute la page — le portail le pose en fin de document — et, refermé alors
que le focus y était, il le rend au déclencheur.

C'est l'application qui tient l'état lu / non lu : le composant ne fait qu'appeler
`onToggleRead` et `onMarkAllRead`.

icon.name: icon
icon.description: Icône du déclencheur. Défaut : une cloche.

label.name: label
label.description:
Nom du déclencheur pour les lecteurs d'écran, et titre par défaut du panneau. Défaut :
« Notifications ».

badge.name: badge
badge.description: Pastille du déclencheur : le nombre de non-lus, ou un simple point. Défaut : `"count"`.

unreadCount.name: unreadCount
unreadCount.description: Nombre de non-lus annoncé par la pastille. Par défaut, celui des éléments `unread`.

title.name: title
title.description: Titre de l'en-tête du panneau ; `null` retire l'en-tête. Défaut : `label`.

onItemClick.name: onItemClick
onItemClick.description: Appelé au clic sur un élément, après son propre `onClick`.

onToggleRead.name: onToggleRead
onToggleRead.description: Fait du point de chaque élément un bouton qui bascule lu / non lu.

onMarkAllRead.name: onMarkAllRead
onMarkAllRead.description: Affiche dans le pied le bouton « Tout marquer comme lu » (tant qu'il reste des non-lus).

footer.name: footer
footer.description:
Contenu libre du pied, à côté de « Tout marquer comme lu » — un lien « Toutes les
notifications ».

emptyText.name: emptyText
emptyText.description: Affiché à la place de la liste quand `items` est vide.

closeOnItemClick.name: closeOnItemClick
closeOnItemClick.description: Ferme le panneau au clic sur un élément. Défaut : true.

width.name: width
width.description: Largeur du panneau, en px. Défaut : 400.

maxHeight.name: maxHeight
maxHeight.description: Hauteur maximale de la liste avant qu'elle ne défile, en px. Défaut : 340.

PortfolioSummaryWidget.description: Ready-to-drop portfolio overview: a big value + delta over a zoomable history chart.

delta.name: delta
delta.description: Signed percent change, shown as a `PriceChangeTag` next to `value`.

series.name: series
series.description: History used to draw the area chart below the headline figure.

WatchlistWidget.description: Ready-to-drop watchlist: a titled card stacking `HoldingCard` rows.

MarketMoversWidget.description: Ready-to-drop "top movers" card: tabbed gainers/losers lists.

SidebarLayout.description:
App shell with a persistent left sidebar on desktop that collapses to an
off-canvas drawer (hamburger-triggered) below the tablet breakpoint.

footer.name: footer
footer.description: Rendered pinned to the bottom of the sidebar — typically a `UserMenu`.

header.name: header
header.description: Optional bar above the page content — breadcrumbs, page title, actions.

stickyHeader.name: stickyHeader
stickyHeader.description:
Keeps `header` pinned to the top of the viewport while the page scrolls (opaque background), and on
narrow screens the mobile bar (menu button + logo) too. Default false.

variant.name: variant
variant.description:
`"default"` : la barre latérale est dans le flux de la page, toujours dépliée.

`"rail"` : la barre est fixée à la fenêtre — elle ne défile pas avec la page — et réduite à une
colonne d'icônes. Elle s'ouvre par-dessus le contenu au survol ou au focus clavier, et le
bouton d'épingle de son en-tête la garde ouverte (le contenu se décale alors). Chaque entrée y
montre son libellé à gauche et sa vignette — `icon`, ou `abbr` pour une sous-entrée — dans la
colonne de droite, la seule visible quand la barre est réduite. Sous la largeur tablette, les
deux variantes deviennent le même tiroir.

defaultPinned.name: defaultPinned
defaultPinned.description: Variante `rail` : état initial de l'épingle quand `pinned` n'est pas fourni. Défaut : false.

HeaderLayout.description: App shell with a sticky horizontal top nav; collapses into a hamburger drawer on narrow screens.

LoginPage.description:
Full-page login layout: a full-bleed image over 3/4 of the width, and a
vertically centered credentials panel in the remaining quarter. Below the
tablet breakpoint the image is dropped and the panel takes the full page.

children.name: children
children.description: The actual form — Input/InputPassword/Button etc. Left fully to the consumer.

SignUpPage.description:
Full-page sign-up layout — same shell as `LoginPage` (image over 3/4 of the width, a vertically
centered panel in the remaining quarter, image dropped below the tablet breakpoint), with an
extra slot for a terms-of-service acknowledgement above the footer.

children.name: children
children.description: The actual form — Input/InputPassword/Checkbox/Button etc. Left fully to the consumer.

terms.name: terms
terms.description: Terms-of-service checkbox or similar, rendered between the form and the footer.

NotFoundPage.description: Centered 404 page with an optional custom illustration and a way back.
